 Germie Bernard Is the WR2 the Steelers Have Been Searching For
 Originally posted on
 Athlon Sports 
  | 
 By Jobe Morrison
  | 
 Last updated Nov 9, 2026 5:00 PM ET
 Add us as a preferred source on Google
 The Pittsburgh Steelers have been searching for an answer opposite George Pickens and then DK Metcalf since 2024. Pickens was traded to Dallas after the Steelers acquired Metcalf, which left Pittsburgh with the same problem at wide receiver. Now it looks like the Steelers have finally found their answer in second-round pick Germie Bernard .
 The rookie earned more snaps after injuries to two of the Steelers’ top four receivers. It hasn’t been perfect, and he hasn’t put up video game numbers. But Bernard has proven to be a reliable target for Aaron Rodgers and keeps making plays for this offense. He has also taken over the WR2 spot, and he isn’t giving it up anytime soon.
 Bernard Thriving as Pittsburgh’s No. 2 Receiver
 Bernard has 32 receptions for 284 yards and a touchdown this season . At his current pace, he’d finish with roughly 68 catches and more than 600 receiving yards. Pittsburgh hasn’t had a second-leading wide receiver top 600 yards since 2023. Bernard has also become an excellent receiver after the catch.
 Of his 284 receiving yards, 174 have come after the catch. He has picked up 14 first downs, and Pittsburgh ranks eighth in the NFL in third-down conversion rate over the past three weeks. Bernard’s performance has been especially critical given Metcalf’s struggles early in the season. As the second half of the season gets underway, Bernard’s importance will only grow.
 Bernard Must Continue His Trajectory
 Oct 18, 2026; Tampa, Florida, USA; Pittsburgh Steelers wide receiver Germie Bernard (17) scores a /td/ during overtime against the Tampa Bay Buccaneers at Raymond James Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Morgan Tencza-Imagn Images
 Realistically, Bernard’s ceiling is a top-tier WR2 and, at best, a reliable fill-in WR1. He hasn’t reached that level yet, but he has shown his floor might be higher than anticipated. The advanced analytics show the kind of production that can get fans excited about his potential. Among Steelers receivers with at least 50 routes, he leads with 3.6 yards of separation per target .
 He also leads Steelers receivers with at least 100 routes with a +4.0% catch rate over expected. Simply put, Bernard is getting open and is reliable when targeted. There’s still plenty of room for improvement, but the early returns indicate the Steelers must make him a priority in this offense. They have finally found their WR2.
